query: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and elevated temperature but a relatively high density of 10.21 g cm−3. What single intervention could reduce its density without sacrificing its mechanical properties at room temperature and at elevated temperatures, including approximately 1000 °C? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict directional changes relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, define the applicable temperature and loading boundaries, identify supporting prior evidence, and propose an experiment and rejection criterion that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Partially substituting the heavy Hf component with a lighter element such as Nb in the as‐cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy will reduce the overall density while preserving (and potentially enhancing) the high room‐temperature and elevated-temperature (≈1000 °C) mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: As‐cast equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr high-entropy alloy with a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³ and high strength.
generation.intervention: Modify the alloy composition by replacing a portion of Hf with Nb, for example adopting a formulation like Hf0.5Nb0.5MoTaTiZr.
generation.conditions: Performance is evaluated under ambient conditions and at elevated temperatures up to approximately 1000 °C, under typical mechanical loading conditions (tension/compression) encountered in high-strength applications.
generation.structural_mediator: The substitution causes subtle changes in lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening, preserving a single-phase BCC (or similarly simple) structure while yielding grain refinement comparable to processing routes such as laser melting deposition.
generation.mechanism: Replacing the high-density Hf (atomic weight ~178.5) with lower-density Nb (atomic weight ~92.9) reduces the overall alloy density. The atomic size mismatch between Nb and the remaining elements sustains or even enhances solid-solution strengthening, thus maintaining or improving the mechanical properties at both room temperature and near 1000 °C.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable reduction in density relative to 10.21 g/cm³ with yield and tensile strengths at room temperature and at elevated temperatures (up to 1000 °C) remaining comparable to or exceeding those of the as‐cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy.
generation.baseline: The as-cast HfMoTaTiZr alloy exhibiting ~10.21 g/cm³ density and high strength performance at room and elevated temperatures.
generation.boundary: This intervention is expected to be effective in as-cast or similarly processed HEAs that maintain a single-phase microstructure and within the tested temperature range (room temperature to ≈1000 °C) under quasi-static mechanical loading.
generation.uncertainty: While molecular dynamics and microstructural evidence suggest that reducing Hf may improve strength, the long-term phase stability and mechanical behavior at high temperatures of the Nb-substituted alloy remain to be fully validated.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize a series of alloys with systematic substitution of Hf by Nb (e.g., Hf1-xNbxMoTaTiZr for x = 0, 0.25, 0.5, and 0.75) using consistent casting methods. Measure density, perform phase characterization (XRD), and test mechanical properties (yield strength, tensile strength) at both room temperature and around 1000 °C.
measurements: Yield and tensile strength at room temperature and ~1000 °C
Phase structure and microstructure (via XRD, SEM, TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If an Nb-substituted alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in density compared to 10.21 g/cm³, or if its yield/tensile strength at room temperature or ~1000 °C drops by more than 10% relative to the as-cast HfMoTaTiZr baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.

## Abstract
High-entropy alloy (HEA) is a new type of multi-principal alloy material and the Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr HEAs have attracted more and more attention from researchers due to their high melting point, special plasticity, and excellent corrosion resistance. In this paper, in order to reduce the density of the alloy and maintain the strength of the Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr HEAs, the effects of high-density elements Hf and Ta on the properties of HEAs were explored for the first time based on molecular dynamics simulations. A low-density and high-strength Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr HEA suitable for laser melting deposition was designed and formed. Studies have shown that the decrease in the proportion of Ta element reduces the strength of HEA, while the decrease in Hf element increases the strength of HEA. The simultaneous decrease in the ratio of Hf and Ta elements reduces the elastic modulus and strength of HEA and leads to the coarsening of the alloy microstructure. The application of laser melting deposition (LMD) technology refines the grains and effectively solves the coarsening problem.
